title: The Envelope
concept:
In Module 2 you briefly met the ADSR Envelope when shaping amplitude. Now let's look at it properly.

An envelope is a control signal that changes shape over time in response to a trigger — in our case, a key press. ADSR stands for the four stages of that shape:

Attack — the time it takes to rise from silence to full level after the key is pressed.
Decay — the time it takes to fall from full level down to the Sustain level.
Sustain — the level held as long as the key is held down (not a time, but a level).
Release — the time it takes to fall back to silence after the key is released.

The envelope generates a CV signal that follows this shape. By connecting that CV to a VCA, you control how the volume of a note evolves — from percussive clicks to slow swells and long fades.

This patch has a complete signal chain: Keyboard → Oscillator → Filter → VCA → Master Output, with ADSR controlling the VCA. Press a key and listen carefully — notice the attack, the sustain while you hold, and the release tail after you let go.

task.instruction: Press and hold a key, then release it. Listen for the four stages: the note rises (Attack), settles (Decay → Sustain), then fades after you release (Release). Try holding different lengths of time.
